case.narrative: This scenario matches MUTCD 11th Ed. Part 6 TA-10 (the federal standard for flagger-controlled alternating one-way traffic on a 2-lane undivided highway). CDOT S-630-1 does not include a general flagger one-lane two-way case; Case 17 (lane closure at a curve) is the closest CDOT analog but is curve-specialized.
case.narrative_2: The generated plan follows the same device layout as the reference case with spacing computed for 45 mph.

fines_double.citation: CDOT S-630-1 (July 2026) Sheet 12, Fines Double Signing Notes

envelope.geometry_note: CDOT Case 42 chain-insertion geometry: R2-10 sits 260 ft upstream of W20-4 in each approach chain (W20-1 moves to R2-10 + C); exit per Case 17 — 500 ft past the downstream taper end to R2-11, 500 ft further to the restoration R2-1. The Case-11 generic formula (wz_start + 500) is not used for flagger: it would collide with the flagger station and violate Sheet 12 note 4's 250 ft sign spacing.

fines_double.gating: S-630-1 Sheet 12 gates Fines Double signing on worker presence in the roadway/clear zone or hazards in the travelway/shoulders/clear zone; LANE CLOSURE is a listed qualifying hazard and Sheet 12 carries no road-class scoping. A reduced-speed flagger lane closure on a 2-lane undivided road meets the gating.

operational_notes.action: Install Fines Double signs no more than 4 hours before the start of the work day. Do not leave signs up overnight when work is not active.
Remove or cover Fines Double signs when work concludes; doubled fines apply only when workers or work activity are present in the zone.
Relocate the R2-10/R2-11 envelope to follow the actual work area as the project progresses; do not leave Fines Double signs in place beyond the active work zone.
Maintain a 250 ft minimum spacing between Fines Double signs (R2-10, R2-11, G20-5P/R2-6P assemblies) and other warning or regulatory signs. Engineer may adjust placement to satisfy this minimum.

flagger.narrative: Two flagger stations are required for alternating one-way operations: one 100 ft upstream of the one-lane two-way taper (MUTCD Fig. 6P-10 50-100 ft band) to stop right-direction traffic, one 300 ft past the work-area end (CDOT S-630-1 Case 17 "200' TO 300'" standoff) to stop opposing traffic.  Flagger stations should be visible to approaching drivers from the full advance-warning distance.
flagger.source: MUTCD 11th Ed. Chapter 6D (Flagger Control) and Chapter 6E (One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control).

spacing.downstream_count_text: Downstream taper: 50 ft at ~12.5 ft spacing -> 4 cones (MUTCD Sec 6B.08: 50-100 ft downstream taper); 7 tangent + 4 downstream = 11 cones total
spacing.in_taper_text: 20 ft spacing in the one-lane two-way taper (MUTCD Sec 6B.08: approximately 20 ft, taper-specific guidance overriding the Sec 6K.01 speed-based rule)
spacing.on_tangent_text: 45 mph -> 90 ft spacing (MUTCD Sec 6K.01: spacing equals 2x speed in feet)
spacing.source: MUTCD 11th Ed. Sec 6B.08 (one-lane two-way taper) + Sec 6K.01 (tangent)
spacing.tangent_count_text: 500 ft / 90 ft max spacing -> 7 cones at 83.3 ft intervals
spacing.taper_count_text: one-lane two-way taper = 100 ft / 20 ft max spacing -> 6 drums at 20.0 ft intervals

taper.L_calc_text: One-lane two-way taper = 100 ft (Sec 6B.08 50-100 ft band)
taper.L_third_calc_text: Required: 100 ft (one-lane two-way taper, 50-100 ft band per MUTCD Sec 6B.08; plan uses the 100 ft maximum)
taper.cdot_reference: MUTCD 11th Ed. Part 6 TA-10 (flagger-controlled one-lane two-way operation)
taper.formula_choice: Flagger alternating-flow: one-lane two-way taper (50-100 ft fixed band per MUTCD Sec 6B.08) -> using 100 ft maximum; the merging-taper L = W x S formula does not apply
taper.source: MUTCD 11th Ed. Sec 6B.08 (one-lane, two-way traffic control): 50-100 ft taper with channelizing devices at approximately 20 ft spacing. CDOT S-630-1 Case 17 warns the taper must be short enough to not be mistaken for a transition.
